; establish each array start, while the earliest resource pointer bounds the end. Arrays have
; different lengths and may be shared; state bounds are contextual, not a uniform32-state claim.
; Physical [8959,10798): Movement/animation stream corpus selected through the preceding pointer
; arrays. Consumers distinguish signed movement/duration records from command-nibble controls and
; animation records. Repeated low-domain patterns and exact neighboring handler boundary were checked.
; Individual record extents and original animation/motion names remain unresolved.
; No-op state entry. The following contact entry checks newly pressed bit 2 before either ordinary
; player/object contact or a forced player-state change; the exact input purpose is unresolved.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AA1E.
; Clear object stream cursors, select horizontal stream 1, vertical stream 0 and animation 1 and
; advance the object state. The paired walking states sample the map at offsets 16,16, stop vertical
; movement on support and route contact to state 3.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AA46.
; Start motion 4 and animation 56. Relative player X differences of0,32 or128 switch to animation
; 4/motion 0; animation 56 restores motion 4. All paths share contact handling.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AAAA.
; Start motion 2, animation 5. A visible object compares half the horizontal player distance with
; vertical separation before starting vertical stream 5 and animation 6; player contact switches to
; state 3.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AB0C.
; Start motion 16/animation 34. The following mirrored patrol states probe both horizontal sides,
; reverse on map boundaries, and sometimes switch to vertical movement when the player lies in a
; narrow horizontal window. Random low bits vary the decision; contact selects state 5.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AB71.
; Probe at offsets 15,16 or15,0 according to facing. A nonzero correction subtracts from working Y,
; resets cursors and restores the corresponding walking motion 16/17 and animation 34/35. Other paths
; retain the common contact response.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AC73.
; Start vertical stream 13 with motion 29 and animation 38. Paired states probe offsets 15,8 and16,13,
; subtract the returned Y correction, then alternate motion 28/29 and animations39/38. Contact selects
; state 3.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $ACDD.
; Start motion 31, vertical stream 14 and animation 41, then advance state. Its active state only
; checks player contact and selects state 2 on a hit.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AD5A.
; Set persistent update bit 7, clear motion streams and start animation 42. A visible object uses
; player X separation and random low bits to choose animation 43/motion 32/vertical 15; a later map
; correction returns it to the stationary state. Contact handling is shared.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AD7E.
; Initialize motion 33/vertical 17/animation 44 and a zero emission cooldown. At vertical state 18,
; require visibility and a player position window before allocating a slot, configuring type 27 and
; placing it at source X+16,Y-2. Sound 49 accompanies emission; a 16-frame cooldown limits repeats.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AE0E.
; Start the same motion 33/vertical 17/animation 44 without resetting the auxiliary byte. The trigger
; requires X within128..207, ahead of the player and eligible for object-group contact. It clears
; qualifying other objects, starts a timed sequence and selects resources32/47.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AEA3.
; After the48-frame delay, start vertical 54/animation 45. Reaching Y<96 stops vertical movement and
; starts a 20-frame burst window. Every32nd frame a free slot1..15 may receive type 4 with randomized
; horizontal/vertical streams at source X-4,Y+20. After the burst, the source exits below Y 208 and
; releases scene control.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AF03.
; Test bounding-box overlap between player and current object. On contact increment the count
; modulo20, award an extra life on rollover, remove the object and request collection sounds. Counter
; units are not identified.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AFCE.
; Enable display bit 2 and start animation 3 with zero motion. Every fourth frame, a visible object in
; the player-relative X window can clear other objects and begin a linked emission sequence.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $AFFB.
; At Y 96, select animation 24/motion 30, find an empty slot1..15 and create type 3 with state 7 and
; animation 61 at source X-16,Y. Save its slot in the source auxiliary byte, request sound 50 and
; advance the source state.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B060.
; Read the saved child slot. When the child disappears or starts vertical movement, stop the parent
; and wait32 frames after animation 40. Resume motion 30/animation 23, then use paired map probes to
; alternate falling and supported states. Offscreen flags remove the source and release the scene
; lock.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B0D2.
; Probe below the object to start or stop vertical movement, then test overlap with the player.
; Contact increments player lives, removes the object and requests sound 33. Correct working Y by the
; collision displacement on landing.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B16D.
; Scan slots1..15. Types5 and above become type 30 with zero state/motion and animation 31; empty and
; lower types are preserved. Stream cursors reset for each converted object.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B1CF.
; Set persistent update, motion 34, zero vertical stream and animation 46. Subsequent paired states
; test floor support and player-relative diagonal alignment within24 pixels; random gating chooses
; stationary/diagonal attack animations or opposite motion/vertical 15. Player contact selects state
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B1F8.
; After the vertical cursor reaches10, probe the map and subtract its correction. Y 160 chooses the
; next facing animation 46/47 and motion 34/35. Otherwise terrain values masked byEF distinguish
; special tiles81/82 and select vertical 22/animation 52. Ordinary cases retain shared contact
; processing.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B35B.
; Mirrored terrain probes choose the opposite state when support exists. A small correction below Y 80
; can change horizontal direction; Y<16 falls into the paired descending state. Other outcomes share
; contact handling.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B467.
; Animation 46/47 permits allocating type 26 at source X-8 or X+16,Y+8. Child motion 38/39 and
; vertical 23 encode direction. Request sound 49, restore the source slot, then switch the source to
; the paired opposite animation/motion.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B523.
; Start vertical 10/motion 3/animation 53. Visible overlap sets player flag $20, places the player at
; source X+12,Y+18 and copies horizontal motion/cursor/timer. Both objects share vertical 11, reset
; vertical cursors, and put player in state 11/animation 19. The source waits until player flag $20
; clears before advancing again.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B5C5.
; A supplies a doubled pointer index into the local script table. Decrement the object timer except
; sentinelFF; when it expires read an action byte plus duration, select motion/vertical/animation for
; actions1..5, clear cursors and advance the script cursor by 2. Other actions stop both movement
; streams. Individual script identities remain unresolved.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B653.
; Clear motion, animation and script cursor, set a one-frame timer and advance state. Six short tail-
; call entries supply doubled script indices0,2,4,6,8,10 to the common timed-action decoder.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B6FE.
; Stop player/object motion and camera command, set display flags3, initialize shared encounter
; health/timers and request sound $83. Wait on divided frames, perform fade progression, disable
; rendering and load successive scene maps before restarting display.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B738.
; Use local phase0..2 to draw screen maps25 and26 at zero horizontal origin, restoring map index 23
; afterward. Completion clears scroll, resets phase and starts48-frame display flashing.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B7B4.
; Every eighth countdown step alternate PPU mask16/1E and display flags1/3 on object types16..23. At
; completion restore normal rendering, select resources2/11 and start a 24-frame delay.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B7F7.
; Scan slots1..15 and set display flags3 for types whose masked type is16. Restore the active-object X
; index before returning.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B838.
; Scan the same type 16..23 group and set display flags1. This is the complementary flashing pass; the
; low type bits are not changed.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B850.
; After the delay clear display/type for the group, restore the active index, set scene control40 and
; timer 5, and advance two states.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B868.
; Countdown or random choice starts a temporary attack state, saving the prior state. Otherwise test
; scene collision, move toward X 96 with camera command81, periodically queue alternating text/tile
; blocks, and inspect contact against the auxiliary object group. A hit starts animation 55 on that
; object, sound 40 and a 48-frame response while preserving nested return states.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B898.
; Mirror the travel logic toward X 160 with camera commandC1. Random low 6 bits and the shared
; activity/input bytes decide whether to enter the temporary attack state or continue moving.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B989.
; An attack lasts24 ticks, switching queued blocks at countdown20,12,4. At the middle event allocate
; type 28 in slots2..15, randomize its vertical stream and timer, and place it at source X+16,Y+32.
; Failed allocation restarts the attack wait; completion restores the saved state.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $B9BB.
; Count down response time and alternate palette/resource selection every four frames. On expiry
; decrement the six-unit health field; surviving hits restore saved movement/attack state. The final
; hit saves position and creates up to six type 16..21 pieces from paired offset and timer tables,
; then clears type 28/29 objects and begins the transition.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $BAA1.
; Continue flashing until the transition timer expires, disable rendering, redraw map23 at zero scroll
; and call the shared scene refresh. Restore object display and rendering, wait96 frames, then remove
; the encounter controller and enter the shared exit path.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $BBB6.
; Mark encounter activity each frame; timer expiry stops motion and selects animation 32. Before
; expiry continue player-contact checks. The subsequent fragment state waits for animation completion,
; chooses one of four groups of five stream pairs, emits up to five type 29 objects at its position
; and removes the source.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $BC14.
; Increment shared activity while active; offscreen flags $D0 decrement it and remove the fragment. A
; following entry removes offscreen objects without contributing activity.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $BC9A.
; Wait for animation cursorFF, then replace the object with type 31, vertical 8 and zero horizontal
; motion. Source types6 and14 choose animation 57 or a random58/59; other types use the same rare
; alternate choice. Reset state/cursors for the replacement.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $BCB4.
; Probe at 16,8; subtract a nonzero collision displacement from working Y and stop vertical movement.
; The common continuation tests reward contact and dispatches animations57..60 to four shared reward
; handlers; otherwise ordinary contact advances to state 2.
; Physical PRG bank 1; CPU entry $BD06.

; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $A992.
; Use the common map collision probe unless player flag bit 0 suppresses it. The suppressed case
; clears all seven probe results and returns carry clear.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $A993.
; Initialize the player and companion object, then interpret held directions and new button presses.
; Collision samples at several offsets gate movement; motion and animation streams are selected
; independently. The precise raft-specific state meanings remain tentative.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $A9AF.
; Stop player movement, select animation 5/state 3 and start a 32-frame timer. This is the newly
; exposed continuation of the existing player controller.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AB15.
; If the first probe gives no vertical correction, probe again at 31,12. A correction clears vertical
; stream/cursor; otherwise return to the ordinary held-direction selection.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AB67.
; Probe at 16,0 and24,4 when the existing horizontal collision result is zero. Any correction clears
; horizontal motion/cursor before rejoining directional input handling.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $ABB2.
; If player display is absent or has high status bits, normalize display to1 and start the shared fade
; counters3/16; otherwise use a 128-frame wait. After fading and the delay, set player exit flag $08.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $ACCD.
; Decrement the player timer; expiry clears stream cursors, restores animation 1/state 1 and vertical
; 3 with frame-parity cursor. Always restore the current object index before returning.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AD07.
; Probe at 16,8. Terrain type 27..37 selects a motion value from the local lookup indexed by tile
; identifier minus108. Direction bits reflect local coordinates before averaging their low 3 bits into
; stream cursors capped at 7. Every fourth frame held directions additionally nudge player coordinates
; by 2.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AD2D.
; When animation cursor is zero, require overlap with companion slot1 and two clear terrain samples;
; reset the companion, copy its position to the player and clear action flag $80. Otherwise new input
; can allocate a player action object using the action selector. Held directions choose horizontal
; streams21/22 and vertical 21/22; idle restores vertical 3 and Y is capped at 208.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $ADF2.
; Wait for animation 9 cursorFF, allocate the selected action object when possible, then reset player
; animation 2/cursor and state 1 before rejoining normal controller processing.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AF29.
; Two entries choose vertical 25/animation 20 or vertical 26/animation 21. Both clear state/horizontal
; motion, set display 3 and place the child at player X+4,Y-8. Stream cursors reset first.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AF66.
; Reset motion/animation cursors, select initial streams and advance the object state. A following
; short entry centers object1; these are distinct entries sharing a classified interval.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AFA3.
; On seven of every eight frames, supported terrain types27..37 stop the companion and choose
; animation 11/state 3. Otherwise combine two top/bottom probes and three side probes, retaining the
; larger correction, to stop vertical/horizontal streams at terrain and screen edges. Terrain
; direction lookup supplies motion and interpolated stream cursors as for the player.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $AFCB.
; Reset cursors and select animation 21 before advancing the companion state. The adjacent entry
; selects animation 19 and clears animation/horizontal cursors before advancing.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B20E.
; Initialize motion 33 or34/vertical 31/animation 23, or zero horizontal motion with vertical
; 32/animation 24 or vertical 20/animation 17. Active variants share player-contact and object- group-
; hit helpers, choosing state 2 when the latter reports a hit.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B234.
; Clear movement and emission cooldown, start animation 28 and advance state. Mirrored active states
; compare player X, require visibility and a vertical distance window, then select one of three child
; stream pairs. A96-frame cooldown and shared contact response bound emissions.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B2BB.
; Three entries select horizontal streams26..28 and vertical 28..30. A free slot receives type
; 30/display 3/animation 20/state 0 at source X-16,Y+8, sound 49 is requested, and the source switches
; animation 29 with a 96-frame cooldown.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B325.
; Fourth member of the neighboring allocation family. On allocation failure join the shared failure
; exit; otherwise choose horizontal stream $19 and vertical stream $1B before shared initialization. X
; must identify an available object slot after allocation.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B35B.
; Mirror the player-relative test and use horizontal streams30..32 with vertical 28..30. Place the
; child at source X+16,Y+8 and switch the source to animation 31. Map collision can reset the source
; to animation 28/state 1 after a 48-frame pause.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B3B4.
; Mirrored fourth allocation member: choose horizontal stream $1D and vertical stream $1B, or join the
; neighboring allocation-failure exit.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B43D.
; Mirrored initializers choose horizontal38/37, animation 32/33 and zero vertical movement. When
; horizontal separation is below 8, switch to vertical 35 with motion 45/44 and animation 34/35.
; Contact or auxiliary-group hit selects state 2.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B4CE.
; Start a 90-frame stationary animation 36. Expiry begins motion 39/vertical 36/animation 38;
; animation completion stops horizontal movement for 30 frames. The opposite half selects animation 37
; then motion 40/animation 39. Each active phase checks player and auxiliary-group contacts, routing a
; hit to state 7.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B562.
; Start stationary animation 40. Ignore offscreen objects and player states2/5; overlap triggers

; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B663.

; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B8D3.
; Set phase $10, select animation $0D for the saved object slot and emit template 7 at $218C. Append
; the 15-byte local VRAM command record and preserve a zero terminator at the queue cursor.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B8E6.
; Set scene phase to 1 and emit template 8 at $208A.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B91C.
; Set scene phase to 1 and emit template 9 at $210C.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B92F.
; Set phase $10, animation $0E and cursor zero, emit template $0A at $218C and append its 16-byte
; command record with queue terminator.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B942.
; Set scene phase to 1 and emit template $0B at $208A.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B978.
; Preserve scene flag $80, set flag $40 and phase $40, initialize animation $0F and emit template $0C
; at $210C. Append an 11-byte command record and zero-terminate the queue.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B98B.
; Select phase 1 and reuse the template-$0A emission path without resetting object animation.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B9CB.
; Select phase 1 and reuse the template-9 emission path.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B9D3.
; Select phase $10 and animation $0E, then reuse template-8 emission.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B9DB.
; Set phase 1 and reuse template-7 emission without resetting the animation.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $B9EF.
; Set phase $10 and animation $0D, clear its cursor, then reuse template-6 emission.

; Set phase 1 and emit template 5 at $218C.
; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $BA0B.

; Physical PRG bank 3; CPU entry $BAC0.
; Physical [31514,31522): Eight one-byte spawn X positions selected by a masked random index.

; type 31, clearing motion/state. Source type 9/10 chooses special reward animations and a player flag

; Ignore offscreen objects and protected player states2/5. Player overlap invokes the raft player

; the auxiliary group and then overlap against companion slot1; return the selected slot through the
; shared scratch field when established.
